sections.html:
Berwyn is a dense inner-ring suburb in Cook County, packed into 3.90 square miles with Oak Park to the north, Cicero to the east, Stickney to the south, and Lyons, Riverside, North Riverside and Forest Park to the west. It calls itself the City of Homes, and the housing fits: small bungalows on the north side around Roosevelt and Cermak roads, larger houses toward the south, and plenty of duplexes and three-unit buildings in between.

Population is 55,001 as of July 1, 2025, down 3.9 percent from 57,235 in April 2020. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $299,800, 61.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and median gross rent is $1,215.

Before it was settled the area was grassy marshland, with Mud Lake reaching nearly to today's southern border, and the south end flooded often in heavy rain. Buyers' inspectors look hard at basements and sewer laterals. If your house has a history of flooding or sewer backup, pull together repair records and any sewer scope reports before you list.

sections.h2: What the city checks before a transfer
sections.html:
Berwyn handles its own transfer paperwork through the Collections and Licensing office and the Compliance Department at City Hall, 6700 W. 26th Street. The city's checklist for quit claim transfers shows what the offices look at. On a regular sale, ask the same departments which items apply to you.

  • Building: a property inspection is required when all parties are coming off title, and any fines or liens must be paid and open permits closed out.
  • Police: parking tickets and fines must be paid in full.
  • Water: the water bill balance must be current.
  • Collector: bring the original deed that will be recorded with Cook County, the completed Berwyn Declaration form and a payment of $100.00, payable to the City of Berwyn by cash, check, money order or credit card.
  • Trusts and corporations: add the trust agreement or corporate papers only if the property is coming out of the trust or corporation, and add an Attorney's Certification form when someone is added to or removed from title.

City stamps are processed at the counter or by mail. The counter is open Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday from 9 a.m. to half past four, and on Tuesday until half past seven in the evening. A mailed packet needs a return envelope with postage. The Compliance Department number is (708) 788-2660, extensions 6445 or 6449.

Berwyn issues a certificate of compliance and occupancy after a city inspection, and the fee depends on the type of building.

Residential certificate fees
Property typeFee
Single-family house$100.00
Two to three units$125.00
Four to six units$175.00
Each unit over six$70.00

Inspections are scheduled in person at the first-floor Compliance Department window in City Hall. Payment is due when you schedule, with no exceptions. Cash, check, money order and credit cards are accepted. The window opens at 9 a.m. every weekday, closes at 5 p.m. on four of them, and stays open until 8 p.m. on Tuesdays.

An inspection report stays valid for six months from the inspection date. Book it close to your target closing instead of months ahead, or you may pay for a second one. Ask the Compliance Department whether your sale needs a certificate at all, since the answer can depend on the building type and who is on title.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit for past work?
sections.html:
Permits go out at the Building Permits Department until half past four on most weekdays and half past seven on Tuesdays. You can apply in person or email buildingpermits@berwyn-il.gov. Incomplete applications are not sent for director review, so check the forms before you submit.

Homeowners may do some non-commercial repairs themselves under the city's Work By Owner handout, and the city publishes guides on what needs a permit and on hiring contractors. The codes in force include the 2024 International Residential Code, the 2012 International Property Maintenance Code, the Illinois State Plumbing Code 2014 and the 2021 Illinois Energy Conservation Code.

Open permits have to be closed out before a transfer is processed. If a prior owner finished a basement or added a bathroom without a permit, sorting it out can take weeks. Ask for the permit file for your address early, then decide whether to finish the work, credit the buyer or sell as-is to someone who will complete it. Buyers who plan to rehab a property often accept the inspection list as part of an as-is price.

sections.h2: Recording the deed with Cook County
sections.html:
Cook County deeds are recorded by the Clerk's Recording Division at 118 N. Clark Street, Room 120, in person or by mail. The deed needs the property index number (PIN), the full legal description, the property address, a mail-to address, the grantee's name and address, the name and address for future tax bills, and city, state and county transfer tax declarations and stamps or a stated exemption.

The Clerk tells filers to check with the municipality for its own requirements, so Berwyn's declaration and payment are a separate step before recording. Illinois stamps have been $0.75 per $500.00 since September 15, 1989, split into $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county.

Only title companies may e-record deeds that carry consideration. Fully exempt deeds can be e-recorded by other filers. A document that misses the Clerk's format standards is charged an additional fee equal to the normal recording fee, so have the title company or your attorney check the deed before it goes in.

Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year. A reassessment notice shows the PIN, characteristics, estimated market value and assessed value. Residential assessed value equals 10 percent of fair market value, then a state equalizer and exemptions are applied. You can appeal to the Assessor or to the Cook County Board of Review.

The Cook County Treasurer mails two installments a year, and the first installment is exactly 55 percent of the prior year's total. Recent due dates have moved around: tax year 2025 installments were due April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026, and tax year 2024 installments were due March 4, 2025 and December 15, 2025. Read the Treasurer's due-date page or your own bill before you choose a closing day.

Exemptions on file include homeowner, senior citizen, senior assessment freeze, persons with disabilities and home improvement. Check which ones your bill shows, because they affect the proration at closing.

A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting and appraisal, but not the city's steps. The inspection, the water balance, parking fines, open permits and the transfer declaration still apply to a Berwyn house, so start those calls while you compare offers.

A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can agree to finish permit work or repairs after closing. Get that written into the contract, along with who pays for the certificate and the city payment. Ask whether the buyer will close on a date that fits the six-month inspection window.

faqs.q: Does Berwyn require a city inspection to sell my house?
faqs.a: It depends on the transaction, so ask the Compliance Department at (708) 788-2660, extension 6445 or 6449. The quit claim checklist requires an inspection when all parties come off title, and a single-family certificate of compliance and occupancy costs $100.00.

faqs.q: How long is a Berwyn inspection report good for?
faqs.a: Six months from the inspection date. If closing slips past that window, plan on a new inspection and a new fee.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax rate on a Cook County deed?
faqs.a: Illinois stamps run $0.75 per $500.00 of value, made up of $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county. Berwyn adds its own declaration and a city payment, so ask the Collector's office what applies to your transaction.

faqs.q: Where do I pay water and parking fines before closing?
faqs.a: Call the Water Department at (708) 788-2660, extension 6463 or 6466 for the balance, and the Police Department at (708) 795-5600 for parking tickets. Both must be current before the transfer goes through.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Berwyn house with open permits?
faqs.a: Open permits must be closed out for a transfer to be processed. Ask the Building Department for the permit file, then decide whether to finish the work, credit the buyer or sell as-is to a buyer who will complete it.
